correctness.rationale:
All essential inferences, boundary conditions and computations were independently re-executed and hold. (1) Universe: U(197,10,{0,1,2,3,4}) = 50 elements (25 in [0,44], 25 in [100,144]) verified by exact enumeration; same 50-element set serves all six p since max 144 < 173. Triangular bound k(k+1)/2>=p gives lb 19 for p=173,179,181 and 20 for p=191,193,197, verified. (2) Theorem A (interval-gap, pure proof): U(D4) subset [0,44] U [100,144] holds (45-99 excluded by tens/units digit >=5, 145-196 excluded similarly; checked by enumeration). Hence integer sums lie in I1=[0,88], I2=[100,188], I3=[200,288]. For p>=173 only representatives r and r+p can lie in union (r+2p>=346>288, r<200 so r not in I3). Re-derived unions: p=197 -> [0,91] U [100,188], missing 92-99 and 189-196 (16); p=193 -> [0,95] U [100,188], missing 96-99 and 189-192 (8); p=191 -> [0,97] U [100,188], missing 98,99,189,190 (4). Matches DRAFT and verify_cover.py interval_missing(). Cross-check confirmed each forced residue absent from S(U). Logic S(A) subset S(U) and 'any A misses >=1 residue => no basis' is valid. (3) Theorem B (full-universe exact enumeration): reran verify_cover.py ALL PASS <2s and enumerate_U.py; confirmed |S(U)|

=173 valid since |S|<=n(n+1)/2 via unordered-with-replacement map, and |U(D2)|=18 verified. (4) Heuristic records are existence-only and correctly qualified: recomputed best 22-set [0,1,4,14,20,21,32,34,40,41,44,100,103,104,110,112,123,124,130,140,143,144] gives 163/197, subset of U, missing includes all 16 forced residues, <= ceiling 173; all threshold_table.json sa_best_A recomputed to quoted cov and subset of U and <= ceiling; sa_p197_D4_k22.json 20/20 at 163 confirmed; greedy_baseline.py rerun reproduces means (e.g. p197/D4 mean 29.6 min 27 max 32, ceiling 173). DRAFT correctly distinguishes proved (A+B, target FALSE) vs verified-existence-not-optimal (SA interval [163,173]) vs conjecture, with no false optimality over C(50,22). No computation error, no boundary error (str(x) without leading zeros matches definition; r+2p argument handles k<0 since union non-negative).

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison shows no prior result covers the same object+claim. Nearest literature: (a) Nathanson Classical Bases / Bose-Chowla/Singer Theta(sqrt(p)) theory treats unrestricted bases for N/Z_n without digit-alphabet restriction and does not tabulate U(p,10,{0..4}) minima; (b) Maynard primes with restricted digits is asymptotic analytic prime existence via circle method/Fourier, complementary to finite exact 2-sum covering of Z_p, different object (primes vs A+A=Z_p) and method; (c) Hough minimum-modulus covering systems treats distinct-modulus covers of Z, different covering notion (translates a+A vs moduli), same certification standard but disjoint. General thin-basis / cyclic-basis literature gives sqrt asymptotics with loose constants, not exact digit-restricted minima for p<200. The specific 18-cell table (|S(U)|, triangular lb, full-U flag) and interval-gap residue lists (e.g. 92-99/189-196 for 197) are not found in training-data sources and are highly parameter-specific (decimal {0-4}, p in {173,179,181,191,193,197}), so unlikely to duplicate a published record. No priority claim is made by DRAFT (explicit triage disclaimer) and none is endorsed here. Live-web verification was attempted but transport failed (see checked_sources), so this PASS means 'no training-data prior covers claim', not a certified priority claim; residual risk noted.

value.rationale: Correct and narrowly new, but not independently worth finding later. (i) What was assigned as improved explicit upper bound (size<=22 basis, 2 above triangular optimum 20, redundancy 253/197=1.28 suggesting feasibility) is FALSE; replacement is 18-cell non-existence table. Theorem A is a 5-line envelope observation: once [0,44] U [100,144] is noted, gaps follow by r/r+p casework with no further theory. It is not developed into a general lemma (arbitrary alphabets, bases, p), gives only 16/8/4 residues for 3 primes, and would be derived in minutes before any annealing — it reveals poor parameter choice rather than a phenomenon. (ii) Theorem B is brute-force enumeration of <=2500 modular sums per cell (<2s total) for an ad-hoc slice: same 50/32/18-element universes across all p (since max 144<173, only modulus varies), decimal alphabet {0-4} and 6 primes <200 have no demonstrated coding/coin/covering application (coding uses binary/ternary, Maynard link is asymptotic vs finite, tenuous). Values like |S(U)|=165 vs 171 vs 173 are reported without conceptual explanation beyond 'computer says', i.e. a parameter sweep. (iii) Heuristic SA/greedy numbers are explicitly non-optimal by DRAFT's own admission (true k=22 max in [163,173]; companions best-found at 20x200k / 8x80k budgets), so they are unstable algorithm-performance snapshots at arbitrary budgets, not citable maxima; future budgets can improve them up to the known ceiling but never to p, so no later work would search for or cite '163/197 at seeds 1000-1019'. Even ceiling-achieving cases (p197/D3 k20=119=ceiling, p191/D3 k20=111=ceiling) achieve only incomplete ceilings (60%/58%), not bases. (iv) This combines the reject categories: mere parameter substitution (same U, varied modulus; single decimal-alphabet slice) plus small exact enumeration that is explained by scripts but not by theory, with no generalizable insight, no application, and no stable positive record. A future researcher on constrained-alphabet bases would re-derive the interval obstruction in seconds and would not need to retrieve this 6-prime table. Hence fails 'independently worth finding later' even though correct and new.
